clue.text: Enthusiastically welcomed lecturer into academic gathering

indicators.note: gathering read as collecting up and rearranging, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for a lecturer, as on learner plates
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A visiting speaker is warmly received on arrival at a university conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic gathering' looks like a conference, but 'gathering' is the anagram signal: L plus ACADEMIC is rearranged; 'into' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acclaimed is to be greeted with loud public praise, an enthusiastic welcome.

clue.text: A religious doubter, heartless and austere

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the doubter word is removed, its heart taken out

parts.note: a sceptic doubts accepted beliefs, especially religious ones

explanation.surface: A doubting believer is described as cold-hearted and severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes out P, the middle letter of SCEPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic life is one of severe self-denial, which is austere.

clue.text: A male sex fiend's thrown into jail, having no fixed abode?

indicators.note: thrown into says the pieces go inside the prison word

parts.note: can is slang for prison, especially in the US
a perv is slang for a sexual pervert, a sex fiend

explanation.surface: A predatory man is locked up and is left homeless.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a camper van owner lives on the move, so in a sense has no fixed abode.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor home lets its owner live on the road, never in one settled place.

clue.text: Entering ruins of Orleans, one flaps

indicators.note: Entering says the numeral goes inside the scrambled city letters
ruins of says the city name is wrecked and its letters rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone walks into the ruined French city, and one thing flaps about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' scrambles ORLEANS, and 'Entering' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailerons are the hinged surfaces on aircraft wings, a kind of flap that controls roll.

clue.text: Team celebrate breaking men's record

indicators.note: breaking says the pieces break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: men's taken as the adjective male
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
to sing can mean to celebrate in song, praising something

explanation.surface: A side celebrates as it breaks the men's world record.
explanation.walkthrough: A maxi-single was a vinyl or CD single carrying extra tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi-single is a type of gramophone or CD release, so a record.

clue.text: Record some of Vivaldi's concertos

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An album holding some of the Italian composer's concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or CD.

clue.text: FE college employs a tutor

indicators.note: employs read as takes in, so the college word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a tech, short for technical college, is a British further education college

explanation.surface: A further education college hires a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: FE is further education, the British sector for school-leavers' vocational courses.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor someone is to instruct them, a synonym.

clue.text: Sound off at delay getting into holiday accommodation. wanting someone to blame?

indicators.note: getting into says the pieces go inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is shelter on a camping holiday
to rave at someone is to rant or sound off at them
a lag is a delay or time gap

explanation.surface: An angry holidaymaker sounds off about delays reaching their lodgings, looking for someone to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: when a holiday goes wrong, the travel agent is the one people blame. The full stop after 'accommodation' is a print slip for a comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The booking intermediary is the obvious target for complaints when a trip disappoints.

clue.text: See 6
Worker on strike gets dole money

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A striking employee is paid unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is money given free, such as state benefit.

clue.text: Politician visiting old King's Cross buildings

indicators.note: visiting read as staying within, so the politician goes inside

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
MP, Member of Parliament
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: An MP calls at an old area of London around King's Cross station.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross is a London station, but here 'King's' and 'Cross' split: Old King Cole, then X.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex is a group of related buildings, as in a sports complex.

clue.text: Treacherous type? Surprisingly, he's taken in by nark

indicators.note: surprisingly says the following words come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
nark and grass are both British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A man fooled by an informer turns out to be treacherous himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the informer next to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a hidden enemy who betrays a friend.

clue.text: See 10
Penguin loves to follow man

indicators.note: to follow puts the loves after the man

parts.note: a gent is a man
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: A man gets two lots of love after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin of the Antarctic region.

clue.text: Earlier Beatles No 1, English hit

indicators.note: No 1 read as the first letter of the band name, not a chart-topper

parts.note: a forehand is a tennis stroke, a hit

explanation.surface: An early Beatles chart-topper, an English hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beatles No 1' looks like a chart-topping song, but just gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means in advance, earlier.

clue.text: Presbyterian in disguise, going round French city briefly

indicators.note: going round says the disguise word wraps around the shortened city

parts.note: a cover is a disguise or front

indicators.note: briefly says the city name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Nantes is a city in western France

explanation.surface: A Scottish churchgoer in disguise travels around a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' reads like a costume, but 'in' merely links; Covenanters belong to Scottish church history, a fact many solvers will need to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Covenanters were seventeenth-century Scottish Presbyterians who signed covenants defending their church.

clue.text: Appropriate help for the upwardly mobile

definitions.meaning: the verb, to take for oneself, steal
a playful description of an elevator carrying people up

explanation.surface: Help is taken for people climbing the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift is slang for to steal, appropriate; and an elevator carries people up floors.

clue.text: In money I've found motivation

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
taken as the letters with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Money in hand provides a reason to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that drives action, a motivation.

clue.text: In remote setting militia, it turned out, is friendly

indicators.note: setting read as setting around, the distant word holding the rest

parts.note: far means distant, remote

indicators.note: turned out read as thrown out, so those letters are expelled from the militia word

parts.note: taken as written before letters are removed
taken as written as the letters removed

explanation.surface: In a remote spot the militia proved, it seems, quite friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turned out' looks like 'as it happened', but takes IT out of MILITIA, leaving MILIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar means intimate or friendly, as in on familiar terms.

clue.text: Regularly scrounged some ice cream?

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone keeps begging for a little ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream comes served in a cornet, the cone shape, so a cone holds some.

clue.text: Transport mediators in S American capital

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates labour disputes

explanation.surface: Travel arrangements for negotiators in a South American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is a British public body that mediates between employers and unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

clue.text: Grants for rebuilding sea wall on Clacton's front

indicators.note: rebuilding says the letters are reconstructed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: front means the opening letter of the town name joins the pool

explanation.surface: Money is granted to rebuild the sea wall along the seafront at Clacton.
explanation.walkthrough: Clacton is an English seaside town in Essex; 'front' gives its C, added to SEA WALL ON before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are sums granted regularly, so grants.

clue.text: Bizarre rules are mostly meant to be broken

indicators.note: meant to be broken says the letters are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A strange saying: rules are mostly made to be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ARE to AR; 'meant to be broken' scrambles RULES plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and strange, bizarre.

clue.text: Panto cat does a turn with giant dressed up in tights

indicators.note: does a turn says the cat word is turned round

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: in places the turned giant inside the tights word

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a monstrous giant

explanation.surface: In a pantomime, a cat performs alongside a giant in tights.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British Christmas stage show; men in tights are a fixture. TOM reversed gives MOT, OGRE reversed gives ERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional British Christmas pantomime story.

clue.text: Area, say, in Brazilian location, to the north

indicators.note: in places the example inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An area of Brazil, for instance, lies to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' just links, adding N at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or district.

clue.text: See 21
Decent shoes girl exchanged for some trendy gear

indicators.note: exchanged says the letters are traded around into new positions

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A girl trades sensible shoes for fashionable outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Designer clothes are fashionable branded garments, trendy gear.

clue.text: Very hairy person seen in the sauna

indicators.note: seen in says the answer is visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A very hairy man is spotted in the sauna.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Esau, Jacob's brother, was born covered in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible describes this son of Isaac as a hairy man.

clue.text: See 24
Stupid to stray in eastern area for a start

indicators.note: for a start takes the opening letter of the area word

parts.note: to sin is to stray morally

explanation.surface: It is foolish to wander about in an eastern district.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, foolish.

clue.text: Defamatory remark comes to sergeant major's attention

parts.note: SM, sergeant major
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A slanderous comment reaches the sergeant major.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes to' links; 'attention' looks like a parade-ground order.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a damaging, unfounded accusation.

clue.text: Protective coating left on submarine

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: submarine as an adjective means undersea

explanation.surface: A protective coating is left on a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' looks like the vessel, but works as the adjective, beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Underseal is a coating applied under a car to prevent rust.
